A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decomposition of SF6 at high pressures and temperatures leads to elemental amorus sulfur, crystalline carbon fluorides, and amorphous carbon.

the reaction of SF6 with C in a diamond anvil cell at 10–15 GPa and 1500–2500 K leads to elemental amorphic sulfur (Sμ) and CF4-III, and the recovered samples at ambient conditions contain either α-S8, helical Sμ, or a mixture of both.
the decomposition of SF6 is induced by laser heating and the reaction products are amorphous helix sulfur and CF4-III, which can be converted to α-S8 after recovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction products of C with SF6 are very sensitive to the laser power used in the laser heated DAC experiments.

the reaction products of the SF6-C system are not stable at the high temperatures and pressures achieved in laser heated diamond cells and the reaction products can be different depending on experimental conditions.
the reaction between SF6 and glassy carbon at high pressure and temperature leads to the formation of elemental amorphous sulfur and crystalline α-CF4-III.
